title: Rule out 3,112 equal-mass helper destination swaps at a single frozen BIT chart
body:
## Result

**NO VERIFIED GAIN.** On the 680-owner BIT word used by #7830 and #7863, 3,112 unordered pairs of productive helpers would improve the invoice if their destinations could be exchanged for free. None satisfies both necessary conditions at any of the 636 frozen charts. This rules out 1,979,232 chart/pair combinations for a single local correction.

Before closing-output relabeling, the required change is the binary rank-one operator ttᵀ for t = eᵢ + eⱼ. The correction chart must be able to read t and inject t into the outputs. We grant every arrival and every send response over the whole tape, even when chronology prevents their joint use. Failure under that relaxation excludes every clock at the chart. The edit keeps the 2,874 paid packet routes, main ports and caller events fixed. Repairs using two charts, changed paid equations, and unequal-mass exchanges remain open.

## Task and overlap

This refines the p104-side-correction task on main e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. The word comes from #7786 at 89a67c404226d51028e135de2b9169e9020d57af. Its canonical SHA-256 is d3aa4426fa8fe7dc167270d01f2515184f2bff6a82744a14e941c5dd3afca27d. ORIGINS.json pins each input by repository, commit, path, blob and SHA-256. This PR registers the exclusion previously published on the campaign fork. [Initial public checkpoint](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19777560)

- #8002 at c2d2fa15fd2ba57d67bbb5b437657620203e8b98 interchanges **paid sender charts and expressions**. Here the exchanged labels are **productive helper destinations** and the paid itinerary is frozen.
- #7970 tests grade-preserving basis changes and a terminal exchange on 679 owners. This package screens strictly profitable equal-mass exchanges on 680 owners.
- #7953 bounds the cost of replacing arrivals at one sink, including same-start retargets. #7985 allows changed terminal decoders after packet omissions. #7833 studies paid-ingress repairs at selected receivers. The new obstruction applies to a correction at any internal or terminal chart.

## Validation

From a clean checkout with CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -IB scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-helper-exchange-obstruction
```

The graph verifier and an independent implementation using the literal forward and adjoint tapes matched the ordered pair digest, per-chart ranks and all 1,979,232 decisions. The literal replay checked all 680 public input columns and 3,554 dirty retirements in each direction. Both scientific checks passed again before submission. Local onboarding ran 760 tests with 31 skips and no failures. The unchanged five-file #7257 CI and historical-replay prerequisite is isolated in 0618e75a22cec54d1651394ef83d088551b7f026. The research package is 8bd02daca9f4e7a227f6c552905930eed9498655.

## Credit and next question

Clear1nsight supplied the #7786 word, #7830 supplier and literal tape engine. Ali Romman supplied the #7776 graph extractor and endpoint checks. We reused the #7781 helper-birth and #6834/#6980/#7001 paired-caller lineage. OpenAI Codex materially assisted the proof, implementation and replay.

The initial one-bridge follow-up in the README has since been priced in the Rounds 311–320 handoff. A remaining question is whether two named, causally compatible correction charts can implement a profitable transposition after charging the connection and restoring both independent returns. [Follow-up receipts and exact open scopes](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/tree/43a72a325f98a2c9bf65f0e92f7e644429b9b3ef)
